questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a result of riding in cold weather for a long time?
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and the lane next to you.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Always use the same lane position.
Change lane positions often to stay alert.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. The safest lane position changes too. Choose the position that gives you the most space and makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: A helmet should NOT:

options.text: Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly all around, and has no visible damage. Replace any helmet that was involved in a crash.

questions.question: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle jumps forward and the rear tire may skid.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle jumps forward and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear when you are not going slowly enough, the motorcycle will lurch forward and the rear tire may skid.

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated when their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at least:
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. Riding under the influence of alcohol is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do?

options.text: Changes positions in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.
Stays in one part of the lane at all times.
Weaves back and forth in the lane to be seen.
Only rides on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes positions in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has three lane position choices within their lane. Pick the safest position based on the current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use headlights from other vehicles to see ahead. Use your high beam headlight, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: Which colors make riders easiest to see?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help a rider be more visible?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To improve visibility, wear bright clothing with reflective material, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow all signs like this.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and ride toward it slowly. Then speed up and ride away.

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: You may have a difficult time getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in a spot the driver cannot see. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your way to escape if something dangerous happens.

questions.question: Riding directly next to another vehicle:

options.text: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
Is better than riding behind the other vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another vehicle. You may be in a spot the driver cannot see. If the driver cannot see you, they may move into your lane without warning. Riding next to a vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: A helmet will not give you the best protection if:

options.text: It is certified by the DOT.

questions.explanation: A good helmet must be certified by the DOT and fit snugly around your head. It should have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Studies show motorcycles with headlights on during the day are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than when headlights are off.
Less safe than when headlights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than when headlights are off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride to help other drivers see you. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed during the day.
